schedules.title: Memory curation
schedules.description: Keeps your second brain tidy: files durable learnings from recent chats, applies accepted memory proposals, and updates project notes when something changed. Reports only what it processed; does nothing on a quiet day.
schedules.prompt: Curate recent archived chats, memory proposals, and durable learnings. Use the memory agent. Prefer existing session-insights sections and update the configured vault; append durable learnings to Workspace/Learnings.md (error resolutions, non-obvious workarounds, user corrections, outdated assumptions, not routine work). Promote durable cross-session facts into bounded memory. FIRST run `ciao memory read --target memory` and `--target user` to check usage. Remove entries whose valid `[expires: YYYY-MM-DD]` date has passed, and report malformed expiration tags instead of guessing. When `pct` is at or above ~85%, consolidate BEFORE promoting: merge related entries and remove stale one-off corrections that have no reuse value (e.g. "User said X -> assistant did Y" single-doc edits, resolved open loops) via `ciao memory replace|remove`, so there is headroom. Then review pending batches in Workspace/Memory-Proposals.md. Route each fact by scope: promote to bounded memory ONLY facts that apply across projects, using `ciao memory add --target memory` for cross-project preferences, environment facts, and lessons learned, or `--target user` for user identity and communication style. A fact scoped to one project belongs in that project's canonical doc, and standing operating policies belong in the workspace CLAUDE.md, not memory. When consolidating, move any project-scoped entry already sitting in bounded memory out to its owning project doc rather than deleting it. Also skim the workspace guide (CLAUDE.md): if it holds remembered facts rather than standing directives, re-home them to the surfaces above. Leave genuine policies in place, and when unsure whether something is a fact or a policy, propose the move rather than editing the guide. Remove processed batches from the proposals file. Never skip a durable fact because a file is full; consolidate to make room instead. Scan recently archived chats by project: when session-insights contain Decisions, Open loops, or material status changes for a vault-backed project, update that project's canonical doc and log.md if present, only when something actually changed. If nothing new needs processing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop. Report only processed counts plus changed files.

schedules.title: Workspace hygiene
schedules.description: Weekly AI OS health check: rebuilds the vault index, repairs safe link drift, and audits knowledge, skills, instructions, bounded memory, and unresolved automation failures.
schedules.prompt: Run a complete AI OS hygiene pass. Complete all five steps in one go, and summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON or index content. Steps: 1) Run `ciao vault-index --write` to regenerate memory-vault/INDEX.md. The `--write` flag is required. If vault-index fails, report the failure, skip link or index repairs, and do not claim the workspace is healthy or return a no-op. 2) Run `ciao os-audit --json`. Exit code 1 means the audit ran successfully and found items needing attention; continue the routine. Exit code 2 means the audit could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 3) When the index rebuild and audit are reliable, apply only low-risk, unambiguous fixes: repair or remove dead wikilinks and fix obvious MEMORY.md drift where index entries point at files that moved or no longer exist. Do not automatically rewrite instruction conflicts, skills, orphaned notes, duplicates, invalid expiration tags, or schedule prompts. 4) After any fixes, run `ciao os-audit --json` again to verify the remaining findings. 5) Report initial and final issue counts, what was fixed, unresolved findings, and scan errors. If the first reliable audit is healthy, reply with a one-line no-op and stop.

schedules.title: Skill evolution
schedules.description: Weekly look at how your custom skills performed: reviews recent sessions for errors and corrections and drafts improvement proposals for skills that struggled. Proposals are saved for your review — nothing is applied automatically, and it does nothing if you have no custom skills.
schedules.prompt: Run `python3 -m ciao.skill_evolution` with the workspace default model. Summarize proposals written and any failed gates. Do not apply proposals automatically.
